title: Only Seven PS5 Games Have Crossed 100,000 Physical Sales in the US This Year
excerpt: New Circana data reveals the scale of physical game sales collapse as Sony prepares to halt disc production by January 2028.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Only seven PS5 games sold over 100,000 physical copies in the US in 2026.
  • Digital purchases accounted for 85% of PS5 software sales in early 2026.
  • Sony will stop producing physical game discs by January 2028.
  • Despite backlash, most PlayStation players are adapting to digital gaming.
  • Only seven PS5 games have sold more than 100,000 physical copies in the United States in 2026, according to Circana data.
  • In the week ending July 11, just two PS5 titles exceeded 10,000 physical unit sales.
  • Sony plans to halt PlayStation disc production starting January 2028, and digital purchases now account for 85% of PS5 software sales.
  • A fierce fan backlash has done little to change the underlying market reality driving Sony's decision.

The physical PlayStation game market in the United States is in freefall, and new sales data makes Sony's controversial decision to end disc production look less like corporate overreach and more like an acknowledgment of reality.

According to Circana director Mat Piscatella, only seven PS5 games have sold more than 100,000 physical copies across the entire first half of 2026. In the week ending July 11, just two PS5 titles managed to clear 10,000 boxed units — a number that would have been unremarkable a console generation ago but now represents the ceiling for all but the biggest releases.

The Numbers Behind Sony's Decision

> **"Sony's most recent quarterly financials show that 85% of PS5 software purchases were made digitally in the quarter ending March 31, 2026, up from 80% the previous year."**

"Sony's most recent quarterly financials show that 85% of PS5 software purchases were made digitally in the quarter ending March 31, 2026, up from 80% the previous year."

The data arrives at a volatile moment for PlayStation. Sony announced in early July that it would cease manufacturing physical game discs starting January 2028, effectively confirming the PS6 will be a digital-only console. The announcement triggered a sustained backlash across social media, with fans flooding PlayStation's posts with criticism and even targeting indie developers who expressed support for the shift.

But the financial picture tells a different story. Sony's most recent quarterly financials show that 85% of PS5 software purchases were made digitally in the quarter ending March 31, 2026, up from 80% the previous year. Physical game sales generated roughly $109 million in revenue during that period, compared to approximately $1.5 billion from digital sales.

"To adapt to consumer trends as the general preference for digital media significantly outpaces physical discs."

— Sony, announcing the end of disc production

While Piscatella did not name the seven titles that crossed the 100,000-unit threshold, industry observers expect them to include 2026's biggest releases: Resident Evil Requiem, Crimson Desert, and 007 First Light. Separate data from Alinea Analytics showed that even the best-performing physical title this year, Ghost of Yōtei, saw only 35.4% of its sales come from disc editions. EA FC 26, the year's top seller by volume, moved a mere 12% of its 5.1 million copies in physical form.

Fan Backlash Meets Market Reality

The backlash has been genuine and intense. Petitions have circulated, developers have faced harassment, and polls suggest roughly a quarter of respondents would consider switching to Xbox over the issue. But a ComicBook.com reader poll found that more than 65% of PlayStation players either plan to stay with the platform or have already gone fully digital.

Game retailers are feeling the squeeze even more acutely. UK chain Game, once a high-street staple, is in financial distress and has blamed the long wait between console generations for its struggles. The company's stores have been reduced to small sections within Sports Direct locations.

What Comes Next

Fan Reactions to Sony's Decision
›25% of players may switch to Xbox.
›65% of players plan to stay with PlayStation.
›Petitions and harassment against developers have increased.

The debate over physical media in gaming mirrors similar transitions in music and film, but with an added wrinkle: digital games cannot be resold, lent, or preserved independently of the platform holder's servers. Game preservation advocates argue that Sony's move puts decades of gaming history at risk.

For now, though, the market has spoken. With GTA 6 confirmed to ship without a disc and physical sales representing a shrinking fraction of revenue, the question is no longer whether physical games will disappear from PlayStation — but whether the remaining 18 months of disc production will be enough to satisfy collectors stocking up for a format's final chapter.
